Messages.Author: Sorrow
Messages.Body:
Why is it that if you use an ability on a weapon (e.g., maneuver on a gun) then you are committed to using that weapon for the next strike but if you use the rush ability on a Talbot's Chainsaw (a weapon) then you are not committed to using it as the next (first) strike in combat? It seems terribly inconsistent to me. The maneuver on a gun and the rush on Talbot's should be treated the same -- they are both capabilities granted by the weapon.

Messages.Author: LivesByProxy
Messages.Body:
Because the designers ran out of text-box space for the line "If you use this ability to enter combat, this vampire's first initial strike that round of combat must be with this weapon."

Which is another way of saying that VTES has horrible layout and graphic design. It really doesn't help that the cards separate effects are not broken up with line-breaks for easy readibility, but in addition to that the elders here love the green marble stripe on the left that takes up 1/6 of the card's real estate.

Gangrel. Noddist. Camarilla. Once each turn, LivesByProxy may burn 1 blood to lose Protean  until the end of the turn and gain your choice of superior Auspex , Obfuscate , or Potence  for the current action.
